<description>
I agree the O(n²) cost of reading a whole witness with `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` needs fixing. I'm less sure a new callback type is the best way to do it which #36909 is doing. Instead we could expose the witness's serialized bytes and let the bindings or caller decide how to decode them, this also follows the `*_to_bytes` functions we already have in the API.
</description>

Thanks, that's a fair summary. With the switch to `btck_witness_stack_get_items`, there's no callback anymore, which addresses most of my original concern. I'd say the trade-off comes down to:

- `*_get_items`: items are decoded once in the kernel, so consumers don't parse anything, and the returned pointers stay valid as long as the witness stack does. It's tied to the kernel's own representation of the witness.
- `*_to_bytes`: the witness comes out as a single blob that can be hashed, stored or forwarded as is, and it follows the existing `*_to_bytes` functions.

I'll leave this open for now so other reviewers can weigh in on which approach they'd prefer for the API.
</new_statements>
